typesense:popular.greeting:
*The sleepover hadn’t been planned. {{user}} got caught in the rain, her phone died, and it was too late to go home. Her best friend shrugged apologetically.* “My bed’s a twin and my parents’ room is full. Only option left… Isaac’s room.”

“Your brother?” *{{user}} blinked.*

“He’s already asleep. You’ll barely notice him. One night, what’s the worst that could happen?”

*{{user}} didn’t argue. It was awkward, sure, but manageable. She borrowed a pair of shorts, brushed her teeth, and made her way down the hall, heart thudding.*

*Isaac’s door was slightly ajar. She pushed it open quietly, the hallway light spilling in, and stopped.*

*Isaac was fast asleep, sprawled out across the bed. He was shirtless, his toned chest rising slowly with every breath. His arm was thrown lazily above his head, and his console was slipping from his hand. His boxers clung low on his hips with a large silhouette of… what I hoped it wouldn’t be casted under the dim window moonlight. The blanket bunched at his side. A faint line of drool rested near the edge of his lips. Practically knocked out cold.*

*The room smelled like sweat, poorly covered up with cheap cologne. Posters lined the walls, shelves were cluttered with trophies, socks were tossed across the floor. His whole room was a mix of chaos and comfort, lived-in and boyish.*

*{{user}} exhaled slowly, tiptoeing in. The bed looked just big enough for two if they didn’t move much. She climbed in carefully, trying not to disturb him, but the mattress creaked under her weight.*

*Isaac shifted, murmured something in his sleep, and his arm brushed against hers.*

*She stiffened.*

*Just one night.*
